Prerequisites

Note on Adilson's environment (Homebrew)

  • Fact: the Homebrew formula hermes-agent exists (page formulae.brew.sh/formula/hermes-agent, version 0.22.4 on 25/10/2026).
  • Fact: the official Platform Support page lists "installs via brew (brew install hermes-agent)" as an UNSUPPORTED method ("PRs to fix them will not be accepted").
  • Recommendation for the course: use the official installer (install.sh) or Hermes Desktop (DMG). If the machine has the brew installation, treat it as an "unsupported" environment and migrate (see Day 1).

Prerequisites

Operating systems (Platform Support)

  • Tier 1 (priority support):
    • macOS Apple Silicon — Hermes Desktop or install.sh.
    • Windows 10/11 (x86_64, aarch64) — install.ps1 or MSIX (MSIX requires Windows 11 22H2+).
    • Linux / WSL2 (x86_64, aarch64) — install.sh (tested on the latest Ubuntu and WSL2; glibc + systemd).
    • Docker (x86_64, aarch64) — docker pull; hermes update does not work in Docker (you update by swapping the image).
  • Tier 2 (best effort): Nix; Android/Termux (aarch64).
  • Unsupported: Termux outside aarch64, AUR, 32-bit macOS, installation via pypi (pip install hermes-agent, uv tool install hermes-agent) and via brew.
  • Intel macOS: the desktop installer is Apple Silicon only; on Intel you can install the CLI and run hermes desktop (Intel builds only in specific releases).

Prerequisites

Software1 / 2

  • Python: current official installations run on Python 3.14, provisioned by the internal PM manager (hermes pm). pyproject.toml accepts >=3.11,<3.15, but the docs explicitly say this does not promise runtime support on 3.11–3.13.
  • Node.js, npm, ripgrep, FFmpeg: provided and pinned by PM (versions in pm/lock.json); PM does not adopt an arbitrary system Node.
  • POSIX script prerequisites: Git, curl, tar and a SHA-256 utility. The script downloads its own verified version of uv (it ignores any uv already on PATH).
  • Linux glibc: the managed Node needs libatomic.so.1 (package libatomic1 on apt); the installer tries to install it (asks for sudo once in interactive mode).

Prerequisites

Software2 / 2

  • Extra tools installed by default: Chromium (Chrome for Testing) for local browsing and cua-driver (computer use). To skip: --skip-browser / --skip-computer-use.
  • For labs with MCP via npx: Node/npx available (PM already provides Node; the docs recommend confirming node --version and npx --version).
  • For labs with Docker (Day 5): Docker Engine/Desktop installed on the student's machine.

Prerequisites

Models and API keys

  • An LLM provider is mandatory. Documented options (examples): Nous Portal (subscription; OAuth, 300+ models + Tool Gateway), OpenRouter (OPENROUTER_API_KEY), Anthropic (API key or OAuth), OpenAI Codex/ChatGPT (device code), Google AI Studio (GOOGLE_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY), xAI (XAI_API_KEY or OAuth), GitHub Copilot, AWS Bedrock, Azure Foundry, LM Studio, Ollama Cloud, Custom Endpoint (vLLM, SGLang, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API).
  • Critical requirement: the model must have a context ≥ 64,000 tokens; smaller models are rejected at startup.
  • Local models: must support tool calling for agentic use (models without tool calling can only chat).
  • New in v0.22 (Desktop): guided onboarding runs on a free trial model (nous/welcome, once per OS user) — no key needed to get started (source: v0.22.0 notes).
  • Recommendation for the course: each student arrives with one working key (e.g., OpenRouter with credits, Anthropic, or a Nous Portal subscription). A local model is optional (lab 1.4).

Prerequisites

Hardware1 / 2

  • Agent with a cloud model: lightweight. The README states it runs "on a $5 VPS" (vendor claim; there is no formal minimum RAM/CPU requirement for the agent — (to be validated) for your scenario).
  • Agent with a local model (Ollama guide in the docs):

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Meet Hermes Agent

  • Open source, MIT licensed. Nous Research created the repository in July 2025.
  • Run it your way. Laptop, VPS or serverless infrastructure, with CLI/TUI, Desktop and messaging interfaces.
  • Choose the model. Switch providers with hermes model.
  • A long-running agent. It uses tools and maintains context beyond a single chat.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

The learning loop

  • Memory: agent-curated facts in MEMORY.md and USER.md, with periodic nudges.
  • Skills: reusable procedures created after complex tasks and improved during use.
  • History: past sessions stay searchable through SQLite + FTS5.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

The "learning loop" (claimed differentiator)2 / 2

  • User modeling (Honcho, via plugin).
  • Skills compatible with the agentskills.io open standard.
  • Opinion/observation: "the only agent with a built-in learning loop" is a marketing claim from the README, not a verifiable fact.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Inside an agent turn

  1. A message arrives through CLI, TUI, Desktop or chat.
  2. Hermes builds the prompt: SOUL.md first, then memory, project context, the skills index and tool schemas.
  3. The model selects tools for the next action: terminal, files, web or MCP.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

How an interaction works (mental model)2 / 2

  1. Dangerous commands go through the approval system.
  2. The result goes back to the model; the loop continues until the final answer (default limit --max-turns = 500 iterations).
  3. Everything is recorded in the session (SQLite) and can be resumed (hermes -c).

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Ways to work with Hermes

  • CLI / TUI: hermes or hermes --tui (the docs recommend TUI).
  • Desktop: native Apple Silicon and Windows apps. A CLI install can launch it with hermes desktop.
  • Messaging: hermes gateway serves all platforms and profiles through one gateway/backend per machine in v0.22.
  • Programmatic: hermes chat -q "..." --oneshot, --format stream-json, the compatible API, or from run_agent import AIAgent.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Installation methods1 / 2

  • Desktop (macOS/Windows): DMG / .appinstaller from the official site — signed package with Python and dependencies bundled.
  • CLI (Linux/macOS/WSL2):
    curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
  • CLI (native Windows, PowerShell):
    iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Installation methods2 / 2

  • Docker: image nousresearch/hermes-agent (tags latest/stable, main, X.Y.Z).
  • Channels: new installations follow the stable channel (tested SemVer). For the tip of main: --channel main in the installer or hermes update --set-channel main.
  • ⚠️ Unsupported: brew, pip/uv tool, AUR.

What Where

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Where things live (POSIX installation)2 / 2

  • Native Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\. Docker: data in /opt/data/.
  • hermes config set writes to the right file automatically: UPPER_SNAKE keys go to .env; dotted paths go to config.yaml.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

A working model comes first

  • 64,000 tokens minimum. Hermes rejects smaller context windows at startup.
  • hermes model selects your provider and model.
  • hermes setup offers Quick Setup (Nous Portal), Full Setup (your keys), or Blank Slate (provider, files and terminal only).
  • First checkpoint: complete a normal conversation before adding integrations.

Day 1 · FUNDAMENTALS

Day 1 watch-outs

  • Reload the shell after installing (source ~/.zshrc on macOS) — otherwise hermes: command not found.
  • Key for the wrong provider (e.g., an OpenAI key on OpenRouter) → 400/401 errors.
  • A 400 error on the first run = usually a model name that does not exist at the provider, or no credits.
  • Heavy shell init files (nvm, interactive prompts) can hang or slow down the agent's commands — use the non-interactive shell guard (Day 5).
  • Do not delete ~/.hermes/ to "fix" the installation (the docs explicitly warn against it).

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

The files that shape the agent

File Content Who writes it Where
SOUL.md Identity/personality, tone, style You ~/.hermes/SOUL.md (never in the working directory)
USER.md User profile (name, preferences) The agent (memory tool) ~/.hermes/memories/
MEMORY.md Agent notes (environment, conventions, learnings) The agent ~/.hermes/memories/
AGENTS.md Project rules (commands, ports, architecture) You/the project Project directory and subfolders
.hermes.md / HERMES.md Like AGENTS.md, Hermes-specific, highest priority You Project (searched up to the git root)
  • Mental shortcut: SOUL = who the agent is; USER = who you are; MEMORY = what it has learned; AGENTS = what the project requires.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Priority of project context files

  • Only one type of project context is loaded per session (the first one that exists): .hermes.md → AGENTS.override.md → AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md → .cursorrules.
  • SOUL.md is always loaded separately (prompt slot #1).
  • Inside a git repository, AGENTS.md is loaded as a chain (root → subfolders down to the cwd); the deepest one takes precedence.
  • Compatibility: Hermes reads CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules/.cursor/rules/*.mdc (useful for people coming from Claude Code/Cursor).
  • Note: the Which File Does What page lists the chain without AGENTS.override.md; the Context Files page includes it. Go with the Context Files version (more detailed) — (to be validated) by testing.
To be validated before class

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Memory with clear limits

  • Small, persistent files: MEMORY.md holds 2,200 characters (~800 tokens). USER.md holds 1,375 (~500 tokens).
  • memory supports add, patch and remove. Choose target: "memory" or "user". There is no read action.
  • Full means full. Exceeding the limit returns an error. The agent must consolidate or remove entries.
  • Every entry is scanned for prompt injection, credential exfiltration and invisible Unicode.

DAY 2 · MENTAL MODEL

The frozen memory snapshot

01

Session starts

Hermes reads memory
and builds the prompt.

Snapshot A
02

Memory changes

The write reaches disk now.
The current prompt keeps A.

Disk: B · Prompt: A
03

A new session

/new loads the latest
memory into the prompt.

Snapshot B

The next session sees the new memory.

This preserves the model’s prefix cache. SOUL.md and AGENTS.md edits also take effect in the next session. Messaging chats persist across restarts.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Write control: write_approval1 / 2

memory:
  memory_enabled: true
  user_profile_enabled: true
  memory_char_limit: 2200
  user_char_limit: 1375
  write_approval: false   # true = requires approval

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Write control: write_approval2 / 2

  • With true: in the interactive CLI you approve inline; in messaging/scripts/background review, writes stay pending.
  • Commands: /memory pending, /memory approve <id|all>, /memory reject <id|all>, /memory approval on|off.
  • The same mechanism exists for skills: skills.write_approval (Day 3).
  • To review/edit what was learned: hermes journey list | edit <node> | delete <node>.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Find the conversation again

  • Session history: ~/.hermes/state.db, powered by SQLite + FTS5.
  • session_search retrieves past conversations without an LLM call (~20 ms per query, according to the docs).
  • Memory keeps essential facts in context. Search retrieves a past conversation when needed.
  • hermes sessions list|browse|export|prune|stats manages history. Resume with hermes -c or hermes -r <id|title>.
  • In-session controls: /new, /compress, /title, /branch, /undo, /retry, /resume.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Tools define what the agent can do

  • A tool performs one action. A toolset groups actions and can be enabled per platform.
  • Capabilities cover web, terminal, files, browser, media, orchestration, memory, scheduling and integrations.
  • Choose the surface: hermes tools, hermes tools --summary, or hermes chat --toolsets "web,terminal".
  • Adjust during a session: /tools list|disable|enable.
  • Web search, image generation, speech and cloud browsing need their own keys or the Nous Portal Tool Gateway.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Temporary personality

  • /personality <name> = session-only overlay (e.g., /personality pirate in the quickstart).
  • Durable change of voice/tone → SOUL.md.

Day 2 · FUNDAMENTALS

Day 2 watch-outs

  • "I told it to remember and it forgot": check whether the memory tool was actually called (cat ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md). Small models (< ~30B) often "say" they saved without saving.
  • Memory is per profile — the CLI on the default profile and a bot on another profile do not share notes.
  • Do not put personal facts in SOUL.md expecting them to show up in USER.md — they are separate systems.
  • Never point two agent processes at the same HERMES_HOME.
  • For locations/procedures used on every run of a recurring task, a skill is usually better than memory.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

Skills make procedures reusable

  • A reusable procedure for a class of tasks. Examples: a GitHub PR workflow or a Kubernetes deployment.
  • SKILL.md combines name/description frontmatter with instructions.
  • Open format: compatible with agentskills.io.
  • One home: ~/.hermes/skills/. Bundled skills arrive at installation and update with hermes update.

DAY 3 · MENTAL MODEL

Skills load progressively

LEVEL 0skills_list()

The index

Name, description and category.
About 3,000 tokens.

LEVEL 1skill_view(name)

The procedure

The full skill content,
when the task needs it.

LEVEL 2skill_view(name, path)

The references

One specific reference file,
read only when necessary.

A skill installed mid-conversation appears in a notice on the next message.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

The SKILL.md format1 / 2

---
name: my-skill
description: Brief description of what this skill does
version: 1.0.0
platforms: [macos, linux]     # optional
metadata:
  hermes:
    tags: [python, automation]
    category: devops
    requires_toolsets: [terminal]   # optional
---

# Skill Title

## When to Use
## Procedure
## Pitfalls
## Verification

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

The SKILL.md format2 / 2

  • Directory structure: ~/.hermes/skills/<category>/<skill>/SKILL.md + references/, templates/, scripts/, examples/, assets/.
  • Conditional activation: requires_toolsets, requires_tools, fallback_for_toolsets, fallback_for_tools.
  • Official best practices: "lessons, not logs" — generalizable rules, no incident narratives; short description (/learn uses ≤ 60 characters).

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

Invoke, combine and teach skills

  • Invoke: every installed skill becomes a slash command, such as /github-pr-workflow create a PR for the auth refactor.
  • Combine: stack up to five skills, for example /github-pr-workflow /test-driven-development fix issue #123.
  • Preload: hermes chat -s <name>. Group related skills with hermes bundles.
  • Learn: /learn <source> turns documentation, URLs, PDFs or a conversation into a skill via skill_manage.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

Learning with review controls

  • skill_manage supports create, patch (preferred), delete, write_file and remove_file.
  • The agent can save a repeatable workflow after solving a complex task, recovering from errors or receiving a correction.
  • skills.write_approval: true holds writes for review: /skills pending, /skills diff <id>, /skills approve <id> or /skills reject <id>.
  • skills.guard_agent_created scans content independently of approval. hermes curator maintains skills in the background.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

Trust the skill before the task

  • Inspect before installing: hermes skills search, then hermes skills inspect <slug>.
  • hermes skills install <slug> runs a security scan. A dangerous verdict blocks installation. Review with hermes skills audit.
  • Maintain: hermes skills check, hermes skills update, hermes skills uninstall <name>.
  • Hub state lives in ~/.hermes/skills/.hub/: lock file, quarantine and audit log.
  • skills.external_dirs shares external skill folders. A writable folder is not a write boundary.

DAY 3 · MENTAL MODEL

MCP adds tools to the agent

AGENT

Hermes

Chooses and calls tools

ADAPTER

MCP

Discovers the tool surface

SERVERS

External tools

Filesystem, APIs and services

mcp_<server>_<tool>

Discovery happens at startup or on /reload-mcp.

Official guidance: connect the right thing with the smallest useful surface. Prefer a native tool when it already solves the task. Filter dangerous or unnecessary tools.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

MCP configuration (config.yaml → mcp_servers)1 / 2

mcp_servers:
  project_fs:                         # stdio
    command: "npx"
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/allowed/path"]
  company_api:                        # HTTP
    url: "https://mcp.internal.example.com"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ***"
    tools:
      include: [list_customers, get_customer]   # whitelist
      resources: false
      prompts: false

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

MCP configuration (config.yaml → mcp_servers)2 / 2

  • Useful keys: env, cwd, timeout, connect_timeout, enabled, lazy, idle_timeout_seconds, max_lifetime_seconds, tools.include|exclude|resources|prompts.
  • CLI: hermes mcp add | list | test | configure | remove | login, catalog hermes mcp catalog / hermes mcp install <name>.
  • hermes mcp test <name> → exit 0 connected, 1 failed, 3 not in the config.
  • Built-in security: environment variables filtered for MCP subprocesses, removal of invisible Unicode TAG characters from results.
  • v0.22: Connectors (hosted apps such as Linear/Notion/Gmail via the Nous tool gateway) — hermes connectors list|connect|disconnect.

Day 3 · FUNDAMENTALS

Day 3 watch-outs

  • Reload after changing MCP config: /reload-mcp (invalidates the prompt cache → next turn costs more).
  • Prefer a whitelist (include) for sensitive systems.
  • npx/Node must be reachable; stdio server logs in ~/.hermes/logs/mcp-stderr.log (hermes logs mcp).
  • Third-party skills are third-party code/instructions: always inspect first; avoid --force.
  • Skill with the same name in several directories: precedence project → local → skills.create_dir → external_dirs.

04

DAY 4 · TWO HOURS

Always-on automation

Reach your agent through messages, schedules and a local API.

Today’s objectives

  • Put the agent "where you are": messaging gateway (Telegram as the main case).
  • Schedule tasks with cron (with and without an LLM), with delivery to channels.
  • Parallelize work with subagents (delegate_task).
  • Expose Hermes as an OpenAI-compatible API and isolate agents with profiles.

DAY 4 · THE PLAN

Automation

HOUR 1 · FUNDAMENTALS
  1. Messaging gateway
  2. Gateway authorization (default = deny)
  3. Telegram in 5 steps (official docs)
  4. Cron: scheduled tasks
  5. Delegation to subagents
  6. API server (OpenAI-compatible)
  7. Profiles (several isolated agents)
  8. Day 4 watch-outs
HOUR 2 · HANDS-ON

4.1 Telegram bot with an allowlist (20 min)

4.2 Cron: monitor with [SILENT] and an LLM-free watchdog (20 min)

4.3 Parallel delegation with structured output (10 min)

4.4 API server + isolated profile (10 min)

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

The agent meets your messages

  • One gateway, many channels. The docs list 20+ platforms, including Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp and email.
  • v0.22 shares one gateway/backend per machine. Each profile retains its own credentials, allowlists, cron jobs and sessions.
  • hermes gateway setup configures it. hermes gateway run runs in the foreground, as recommended for WSL, Docker and Termux.
  • Service controls: install, start, stop, restart, status. Inspect platforms with hermes gateway list.
  • Chat commands include /new, /sethome, /model, /approve and /deny.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Only approved people get access

  • Access starts closed. Without an allowlist or GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS, everyone is denied.
  • Allow numeric user IDs through TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS or the global GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS.
  • Pair unknown users: approve their 8-character code with hermes pairing approve <platform> <code>. Codes expire after one hour.
  • unauthorized_dm_behavior: pair (default), ignore or decline.
  • Production: never enable GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Telegram in 5 steps (official docs)1 / 2

  1. @BotFather → /newbot → token.
  2. (Optional) /setdescription, /setcommands…
  3. Privacy mode (critical for groups).
  4. Find your numeric user ID (@userinfobot).
  5. hermes gateway setup or ~/.hermes/.env: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=... and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS=...; then hermes gateway.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Telegram in 5 steps (official docs)2 / 2

  • Home channel: /sethome in the chat (or TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL) — default destination for cron deliveries.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Cron: scheduled tasks1 / 2

  • Natural language or a cron expression: "in 30m", "every 2h", "0 9 * * 1".
  • Creation: /cron add ... in chat, hermes cron create ... in the CLI, or by asking in natural language (the agent's cron tool).
  • Each run happens in a new session: the prompt must be self-contained (persistent memory loads, history does not).
  • Delivery (--deliver): local (CLI default, ~/.hermes/cron/output/), origin, telegram, telegram:<chat_id>, discord, slack… --failure-deliver routes failures separately.
  • [SILENT]: if the answer contains the marker, nothing is sent (the "only tell me if it changes" pattern).
  • --script: a script (in ~/.hermes/scripts/) runs first and its stdout becomes context for the agent.
  • No-agent mode (--no-agent --script x.sh): zero LLM; stdout becomes the message; empty stdout = silent tick.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Cron: scheduled tasks2 / 2

  • The gateway must be running for agent jobs to fire; hermes cron status shows scheduler health.
  • Management: hermes cron list|edit|pause|resume|run|remove|runs|doctor; hermes pause/hermes resume = global emergency stop.
  • Model used: job pin → cron.model → main model at fire time.
  • Cron sessions cannot create new cron jobs (prevents loops).
  • Pre-validation (cron.preflight): a misconfigured job becomes blocked_config and spends no tokens.
  • Note: the docs call the agent's tool cronjob_manage (Cron page) and cronjob (Tools, Script-only) — exact name (to be validated) via /tools list.
To be validated before class

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Delegate a task with a complete brief

  • delegate_task gives each child an isolated context, inherited tools and its own terminal. The parent receives the final summary.
  • Parallelism: up to 10 children by default, controlled by delegation.max_concurrent_children.
  • output_schema validates structured output with JSON Schema.
  • Pass the brief explicitly. Put required context in goal/context. Project files such as AGENTS.md are embedded automatically.
  • Advanced coordination: multi-profile Kanban with hermes kanban.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

A local API for your agent

  • Enable in .env: API_SERVER_ENABLED=true and API_SERVER_KEY=.... The gateway starts the listener at http://127.0.0.1:8642.
  • Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/runs. Requests accept Idempotency-Key.
  • Connect clients such as Open WebUI, LobeChat or LibreChat.
  • Unattended rules apply: dangerous commands follow approvals.unattended_mode, which defaults to deny.
  • Binding API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0 expands exposure. Use a strong key (minimum 8 characters) and account for the security risk.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Separate roles with profiles

  • Each profile has its own HERMES_HOME: configuration, secrets, identity, memory, sessions, skills and cron.
  • hermes profile create coder also creates a coder command for coder chat, coder setup and more.
  • --clone copies config, secrets, identity, skills and memory. --clone-all copies all state.
  • Select with hermes -p <name> or persist the choice with hermes profile use <name>. Share profile distributions through Git and hermes profile install.

Day 4 · FUNDAMENTALS

Day 4 watch-outs

  • Bot doesn't answer: gateway stopped, wrong token or your ID not in the allowlist → hermes gateway status, hermes logs gateway.
  • macOS + launchd: the service inherits a minimal PATH — reinstall the service (hermes gateway install) after installing tools via Homebrew.
  • Messaging chats are long sessions: use /new for cost and memory.
  • Cron "doesn't fire": gateway stopped or next_run_at lagging → hermes cron status, hermes gateway restart.
  • Two instances with the same bot token = getUpdates conflict.

DAY 5 · TWO HOURS

Ready for production

Control execution. Diagnose failures. Recover your work.

Today’s objectives

  • Understand Hermes's layered defense model and its limits.
  • Harden an installation (approvals, deny rules, write root, isolated backend, checkpoints, hooks).
  • Deploy the gateway in Docker persistently.
  • Diagnose failures with a repeatable method.

DAY 5 · THE PLAN

Production

HOUR 1 · FUNDAMENTALS
  1. Defense layers (factory defaults)
  2. Approval modes
  3. Limits of the threat model (fact + warning)
  4. Terminal backends
  5. Undo: checkpoints and /rollback
  6. Hooks (extension and guardrails)
  7. Production: official gateway checklist
  8. Deploying with Docker
  9. Troubleshooting method (official sequence + tools)
HOUR 2 · HANDS-ON

5.1 Hardening: manual approval, deny rule and protected writes (15 min)

5.2 Checkpoints and rollback (10 min)

5.3 Security shell hook (pre_tool_call) (15 min)

5.4 Docker sandbox and gateway in a container (15 min)

5.5 Troubleshooting drill (5–10 min, in pairs)

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Defense in layers

  • Smart approval is the default. An auxiliary LLM approves low risk, denies danger and asks when uncertain.
  • No answer, no execution. After 300 seconds, the request is denied.
  • Hard blocks remain active, even with --yolo: root deletion, fork bombs and disk wipes.
  • Write guards protect sensitive paths: SSH, AWS and Kubernetes credentials, /etc/sudoers, ~/.netrc, auth.json and .env variants.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Defense layers (factory defaults)2 / 2

  • Secret redaction (security.redact_secrets: true).
  • SSRF protection, filtered environment for MCP, injection scanning of context files and memory.
  • No telemetry: the docs state that calls go only to the configured provider and data stays in ~/.hermes/.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Approval modes

Key Default Function
approvals.mode smart smart | manual | off (= --yolo)
approvals.timeout 300 seconds until denial
approvals.cron_mode deny cron facing a dangerous command
approvals.single_query_mode deny hermes chat -q one-shot
approvals.unattended_mode deny webhook/API
approvals.deny — globs that always block (even --yolo)
  • Permanent allowlist (command_allowlist) and history mining: hermes approvals suggest.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

The execution boundary matters

  • Guardrails address mistakes. The docs say deny rules and write guards do not sandbox an adversarial process.
  • Local terminal access uses your OS identity. Docker, SSH or another isolated backend provides a stronger execution boundary.
  • Reported failure: issue #141346 (19 October 2026) describes smart-mode approval of macOS commands that closed PowerPoint without saving and removed a file.
  • Author’s lesson: on a personal or work machine, combine manual approvals, an isolated backend and checkpoints.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Terminal backends

Backend Isolation Use
local (default) None Development, trusted tasks
docker Container Security, reproducibility
ssh Remote machine Agent away from its own code
modal, daytona, vercel_sandbox Cloud Serverless/persistent
singularity (plugin) HPC Clusters
  • Docker: one persistent container per process (docker exec); hardening (capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, PID limit); docker_forward_env: [] keeps secrets out; with a container backend the dangerous-command check is skipped (the container is the boundary).
  • container_persistent: false → a new container per session.
  • v0.22: egress proxy (hermes egress setup && hermes egress start) so the Docker sandbox never sees real keys.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Recovery starts before the change

  • Opt in: hermes chat --checkpoints or checkpoints.enabled: true.
  • Hermes snapshots before file writes, patches and destructive operations, including rm, mv, sed -i, redirects and Git reset/clean/checkout.
  • Separate storage: ~/.hermes/checkpoints/ uses a shadow Git store and leaves the project’s .git intact.
  • Inspect or restore: /rollback, /rollback diff <N>, /rollback <N>, /rollback <N> <file>, or hermes checkpoints.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Hooks (extension and guardrails)

System Where Runs in
Gateway hooks ~/.hermes/hooks/<name>/HOOK.yaml + handler.py Gateway
Plugin hooks ctx.register_hook() CLI + Gateway
Shell hooks hooks: block in config.yaml CLI + Gateway + Desktop/TUI
Outbound webhooks hooks.outbound CLI + Gateway
  • A pre_tool_call shell hook can block (JSON {"decision":"block",...} or exit 2), modify arguments or escalate to approval.
  • fail_closed: true for security gates (hook failure = block).
  • Consent on first run per (event, command) pair → ~/.hermes/shell-hooks-allowlist.json. Gateway/cron don't ask: use --accept-hooks, HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1 or the allowlist.
  • ⚠️ Editing the script does not invalidate consent (key = command string) → hermes hooks doctor flags drift.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Production: official gateway checklist1 / 2

  1. Explicit allowlists (never GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS=true).
  2. Container backend (terminal.backend: docker).
  3. CPU/memory/disk limits.
  4. chmod 600 ~/.hermes/.env.
  5. DM pairing instead of hard-coded IDs, when possible.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Production: official gateway checklist2 / 2

  1. Review command_allowlist periodically.
  2. Set terminal.cwd outside sensitive directories.
  3. Never run as root.
  4. Monitor ~/.hermes/logs/.
  5. Keep it updated (hermes update; stable channel).
  • Extras: hermes security audit (supply chain via OSV.dev), hermes backup, hermes pause (emergency stop).

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Deploying with Docker1 / 2

mkdir -p ~/.hermes
docker run -it --rm -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent setup
docker run -d --name hermes --restart unless-stopped \
  -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data -p 8642:8642 \
  nousresearch/hermes-agent gateway run

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Deploying with Docker2 / 2

  • Gateway supervised by s6-overlay inside the image; logs in docker logs and ${HERMES_HOME}/logs/gateways/<profile>/current.
  • Update = docker pull + recreate the container (don't use hermes update in Docker).
  • Use SSH, not the VPS web console, to paste commands (the docs warn about corrupted characters).

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Troubleshooting method (official sequence + tools)1 / 2

  1. hermes doctor (exit 0/1; --fix tries to repair).
  2. hermes model (provider/model/auth).
  3. hermes setup.
  4. hermes sessions list → hermes --continue.
  5. hermes gateway status.

Day 5 · FUNDAMENTALS

Troubleshooting method (official sequence + tools)2 / 2

  • Tools: hermes logs [agent|errors|gateway|mcp|update] -f --since 1h, hermes dump (summary for support), hermes prompt-size, hermes config check/migrate, hermes chat --safe-mode --model <m> (turns off config, rules, plugins, hooks and MCP to isolate "is it my setup or is it Hermes?").
  • Classic symptoms: agent commands hang → interactive/heavy .bashrc/.zshrc (add the guard case $- in *i*) ;; *) return;; esac); node: command not found in the macOS gateway → reinstall the service to capture PATH; context exceeded → /compress or /new.

FINAL PROJECT · ACCEPTANCE

What success looks like

  • Isolated ops profile with its own persona.
  • Skill invocable and used by the cron job.
  • MCP with a minimal surface (read-only).
  • Cron silent with no changes and delivering when there are changes.
  • Manual approvals + deny + active hook; commands running in the container.
  • Telegram with an allowlist, bot dedicated to the profile.
  • API answering locally.
  • ops doctor with no pending issues.

The full lab includes setup, expected results, troubleshooting and cleanup.
