← Lab 1.1 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 1

Lab 1.1: Clean installation and diagnostics

Test objective: install Hermes Agent using the supported method and confirm the installation is healthy.

Prerequisites and setup: macOS Apple Silicon or Linux/WSL2; Git and curl; internet access. If a Homebrew installation already exists, check it first (step 1).

Step by step:

  1. Check whether there is a previous installation and where it comes from:
    which hermes
hermes --version
brew list --formula 2>/dev/null | grep -i hermes
    • Expected result: if nothing exists, which returns nothing. If the brew formula hermes-agent shows up, you are on an unsupported method: uninstall it with brew uninstall hermes-agent before continuing (standard Homebrew command; do not keep test config).
  2. Install with the official script:
    curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
    • Expected result: one status line per stage; when run interactively, the script may start setup at the end. Full log in ~/.hermes/logs/install.log.
    • For this lab, if interactive setup opens, you can configure it right away (or exit and do it in Lab 1.2).
  3. Reload the shell:
    source ~/.zshrc   # macOS (zsh)  — ou: source ~/.bashrc
  4. Confirm version and diagnostics:
    hermes --version
hermes doctor
    • Expected result: version 0.22.5 (or newer, if the stable channel moves ahead) — exact output format (to be validated). hermes doctor exits with code 0 if there are no pending issues and 1 if there are.
  5. Inspect the structure that was created:
    ls -la ~/.hermes/
hermes config path
hermes config env-path

Test data/inputs: none.

Success criterion: hermes --version responds; hermes doctor; echo $? shows 0 (or only warnings related to a provider not yet configured).

Common errors and fixes:

Symptom Cause Fix
hermes: command not found Shell not reloaded / PATH source ~/.zshrc or add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
Node installation fails on minimal Linux Missing libatomic.so.1 Install libatomic1 (apt) — the installer error shows the exact command
Chromium download failed Network/platform Installation completes anyway; run hermes pm install chromium later
Missing config after update Outdated config hermes config check and hermes config migrate

Environment cleanup: none (the installation will be used in the next labs). Full uninstall, if needed: hermes uninstall.

Variation/extra challenge: run hermes dump and identify in the output the installation origin (provenance) and the update channel; run hermes update --check to see whether a new version exists without installing it.

← Lab 1.2 overview25 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 1

Lab 1.2: Provider, first conversation with a tool and session resume

Test objective: configure an LLM provider, validate a multi-turn conversation that uses the terminal tool, and resume the session.

Prerequisites and setup: Lab 1.1 completed; an API key (e.g., OpenRouter) or a Nous Portal subscription. Create a working folder:

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day1 && cd ~/hermes-course/day1
echo "# Course demo project" > README.md
printf 'print("hello, hermes")\n' > app.py

Step by step:

  1. Choose the provider:
    hermes model
    • Alternative via Nous Portal: hermes setup --portal.
    • Direct alternative (OpenRouter): hermes config set OPENROUTER_API_KEY sk-or-... and then hermes model to choose the model.
    • Expected result: provider and model saved (hermes config get model.default shows the model).
  2. Confirm where the key ended up (do not show the key on the projector!):
    hermes config get model.default
grep -c OPENROUTER_API_KEY ~/.hermes/.env
  3. Start the TUI:
    hermes --tui
    • Expected result: banner with model/provider, available tools and skills.
  4. Send verifiable prompts (one at a time):
    List the files in this directory and say which appears to be the main file.

    Run app.py and tell me the exact output.
    • Expected result: the agent uses the terminal/file tool, shows the execution and answers hello, hermes.
  5. Try slash commands: /help, /tools, /model (just open and cancel), /usage.
  6. Test interruption: ask for something long ("count from 1 to 500 explaining each number") and, during the answer, type a new message and press Enter (or Ctrl+C).
  7. Exit (/quit) and resume:
    hermes -c
    • Ask: What was the output of the app.py you ran earlier? — the agent should remember (same session).
  8. List sessions:
    hermes sessions list

Test data/inputs: README.md and app.py created during setup.

Expected result per step: (1) model saved; (3) banner OK; (4) visible tool use and correct output; (7) context preserved; (8) session listed.

Success criterion: conversation with more than one turn, at least one successful tool call, and resume via hermes -c with context preserved.

Common errors and fixes:

Symptom Likely cause Fix
HTTP 400 on the first message Model does not exist at the provider / no credits hermes model and pick a valid model; check credits
Empty/broken answers Wrong auth or model hermes model again
Model rejected at startup Context < 64K Pick a model with ≥ 64K context
429 Provider rate limit Wait; switch model/provider (--provider)
hermes -c does not find the session Different profile or session not saved hermes sessions list; confirm the profile
Approval prompt when running a command Approval system (normal) Read the command and approve/deny (covered in depth on Day 5)

Cleanup: keep the configuration. Optional: hermes sessions delete <session-id> for test sessions.

Variation/extra challenge: run in one-shot mode and capture JSONL:

hermes chat --oneshot -q "Say only OK" ; echo "exit=$?"
hermes chat -q "List the .py files in this directory" --format stream-json

Identify the system, tool_use, tool_result and result events in the output.

← Lab 1.3 overview10 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 1

Lab 1.3: File map and configuration

Test objective: know how to read and change configuration safely.

Prerequisites: Labs 1.1–1.2.

Step by step:

  1. hermes config show — see the effective configuration.
  2. hermes config get terminal.backend — expected: local (default).
  3. hermes config set terminal.timeout 240 and hermes config get terminal.timeout — expected: 240.
  4. hermes config unset terminal.timeout — returns to the default (the docs show timeout: 180 as an example).
  5. hermes prompt-size — see how much of the prompt is taken by skills, memory and tools (runs offline).
  6. hermes status and hermes insights — auth/platform status and token/cost analytics.

Success criterion: change and revert a key, and explain the difference between .env and config.yaml.

Common errors: writing a list as a string (e.g., plugins.enabled: '["a"]') — hermes doctor flags it; use a YAML literal (hermes config set <chave> '[a, b]').

Cleanup: none.

Extra challenge: use hermes logs errors -n 20 and hermes logs -f in another terminal while chatting.

← Lab 1.4 overview≈15 min, hardware-dependent

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 1

Lab 1.4: Local model with Ollama

Test objective: run Hermes against a local model through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Prerequisites and setup: Ollama installed (on Mac: the Ollama app; on Linux: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh); a machine with compatible RAM. The docs recommend gemma4:31b (≈20 GB on disk, 24+ GB RAM) as a local option with reliable tool calling. On smaller machines, use another model with tool calling from the Ollama library — suitability (to be validated).

Step by step:

  1. Check Ollama:
    ollama --version
curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags
  2. Download the model and test the endpoint:
    ollama pull gemma4:31b
curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gemma4:31b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], "max_tokens": 50}'
  3. Create a variant with context ≥ 64K (Ollama's default is 2048 tokens):
    mkdir -p ~/.hermes/cache/scratch
cat > ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/Modelfile << 'EOF2'
FROM gemma4:31b
PARAMETER num_ctx 64000
EOF2
ollama create gemma4-64k -f ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/Modelfile
    • Note: the docs use num_ctx 64000, and elsewhere require "at least 64,000 tokens" and suggest 65536 — if Hermes rejects it, use PARAMETER num_ctx 65536 (to be validated).
  4. Configure Hermes via hermes model → Custom Endpoint (Base URL http://localhost:11434/v1, empty key or no-key, model gemma4-64k), or edit ~/.hermes/config.yaml:
    model:
  default: "gemma4-64k"
  provider: "custom"
  base_url: "http://localhost:11434/v1"
  5. For a slow CPU, increase the timeout in ~/.hermes/.env: HERMES_API_TIMEOUT=1800.
  6. Run hermes and ask: List the Python files in this directory and count the lines in each one.

Success criterion: answer with tool use, with no calls to cloud providers.

Common errors:

Symptom Fix
Connection refused Ollama stopped: ollama serve (or open the app)
provider 'ollama' has no endpoint configured Set providers.ollama.base_url: "http://localhost:11434/v1" or use provider: custom with base_url
Agent says "I saved/did it" but didn't Small model/no tool calling — use a larger model
Very slow Model larger than RAM; reduce model/quantization

Cleanup: switch back to the cloud provider with hermes model. Optional: ollama rm gemma4-64k.

Extra challenge: configure a cloud fallback (fallback_providers, see the Ollama guide in the docs) and observe when it kicks in. In Desktop v0.22, compare with Settings → Providers → Local Models (managed llama.cpp).

← Lab 2.1 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 2

Lab 2.1: Persona (SOUL.md) + project rules (AGENTS.md)

Test objective: demonstrate the separation between global identity (SOUL.md) and project rules (AGENTS.md), and when each one is loaded.

Prerequisites and setup:

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day2/project && cd ~/hermes-course/day2/project
git init -q
printf 'def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n' > calc.py
cp ~/.hermes/SOUL.md ~/hermes-course/day2/SOUL.md.bak 2>/dev/null || true

Step by step:

  1. Edit ~/.hermes/SOUL.md (backup already made) and append at the end (the block below sets an English voice, a consistent signature and a five-bullet limit):
    ## Course style
- Always answer in English.
- End every answer with the line: "Hermes (course)".
- Be direct. Use at most 5 bullets.
  2. Create AGENTS.md in the project (rules: Python 3, pytest tests in tests/, every new function needs a docstring in English, never change files outside this directory):
    cat > AGENTS.md << 'EOF2'
# Calc project rules
- Language: Python 3. Tests use pytest in tests/.
- Every new function needs an English docstring.
- Never change files outside this directory.
EOF2
  3. Start a new session in the project directory: hermes
  4. Ask: What are the rules of this project?
    • Expected: the agent quotes the rules from AGENTS.md, in English, ending with "Hermes (course)".
  5. Ask: Create a subtract function in calc.py following the project rules.
    • Expected: function with a docstring in English; possibly a test proposal in tests/.
  6. Test loading at session start: without exiting, edit AGENTS.md adding - Use type hints in all functions. and ask for the rules again. Expected: the new rule does not show up (context assembled at the start). Run /new (or exit and run hermes) and ask again — now it shows up.
  7. Test isolation: cd ~ && hermes chat --oneshot -q "What are the rules of the current project?" — expected: it does not know the calc rules (but keeps the SOUL.md style).
  8. Test without rules: cd ~/hermes-course/day2/project && hermes chat --ignore-rules --oneshot -q "What are the project rules?" — expected: ignores AGENTS.md and SOUL.md.

Success criterion: behavior changes according to directory/session exactly as described in steps 4, 6, 7 and 8.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Rules don't load A higher-priority .hermes.md or CLAUDE.md exists, or wrong cwd Check the context files in the directory
SOUL.md change doesn't show up Old session /new
Empty SOUL.md Fallback to default identity Check content/permissions

Cleanup:

cp ~/hermes-course/day2/SOUL.md.bak ~/.hermes/SOUL.md 2>/dev/null || true

(keep the project for Day 3).

Extra challenge: create AGENTS.override.md in the same directory with a different rule and check whether it replaces AGENTS.md (to be validated — see 4.2). Use /plan Add multiplication with tests and check the plan saved in .hermes/plans/.

← Lab 2.2 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 2

Lab 2.2: Persistent memory, frozen snapshot and approval

Test objective: verify real memory writes, the effect of the frozen snapshot and the write_approval gate.

Prerequisites: Lab 1.2; a model with good tool calling.

Step by step:

  1. Check the current state:
    cat ~/.hermes/memories/USER.md 2>/dev/null; cat ~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md 2>/dev/null
  2. In hermes, ask explicitly (save a concrete preference to the user profile):
    Use the memory tool to save to the user profile: "The course instructor prefers Python examples and English answers".
    • Expected: the agent calls memory with target: "user" (visible in the tool output).
  3. In another terminal: cat ~/.hermes/memories/USER.md — the entry should be in the file.
  4. In the same session, ask What is in your user profile block in the system prompt? — expected: the new entry may not yet appear in the injected block (frozen snapshot), even though the agent knows it from the conversation.
  5. Run /new and ask What preferences do you know about me? — expected: it mentions the saved preference.
  6. Enable the approval gate:
    hermes config set memory.write_approval true
    In a new session, ask: Save to memory that the calc project lives in ~/hermes-course/day2/project. — expected in the interactive CLI: inline approval prompt. Approve or deny and check the file.
  7. Review the "learning":
    hermes journey list

Success criterion: entry present in USER.md; snapshot behavior reproduced; approval gate triggered.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Agent says it saved, file empty Model did not call the tool Explicitly ask "use the memory tool"; use a stronger model
Write "disappeared" It was left pending (gate active outside the CLI) /memory pending → /memory approve all
Limit error Memory full (2,200/1,375 chars) Let the agent consolidate or remove entries
Different file than expected Another profile hermes profile list; profiles use ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/memories/

Cleanup:

hermes config set memory.write_approval false

Remove the test entries with hermes journey delete <node> (ids from hermes journey list) or by asking the agent remove the entry about the calc project from memory.

Extra challenge: in a new session, ask "Did I run an app.py in an earlier conversation? What was the output?" ("In any earlier conversation did I run an app.py? What was the output?") and observe whether the agent uses session_search.

← Lab 2.3 overview15 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 2

Lab 2.3: Restricted toolsets and tool control

Test objective: limit the tool surface and observe the effect.

Step by step:

  1. See the current summary: hermes tools --summary.
  2. Run a session with files only (no terminal):
    cd ~/hermes-course/day2/project
hermes chat --oneshot --toolsets "file" -q "Run calc.py with Python and show the output."
    • Expected: the agent says it cannot run commands (no terminal toolset) or offers to only read the file.
  3. Repeat with --oneshot --toolsets "file,terminal" — now it runs.
  4. Inside a session: /tools list, then /tools disable web (if enabled) and /tools enable web.
  5. Open hermes tools and browse the per-platform configuration (CLI vs. Telegram) without saving.

Success criterion: the same request fails without terminal and works with terminal.

Common errors: wrong toolset name — check the Toolsets Reference; web tool unavailable due to missing key/Tool Gateway.

Cleanup: none (flags apply only to that run).

Extra challenge: use the safe toolset and find out what it includes (see reference/toolsets-reference in the docs).

← Lab 3.1 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 3

Lab 3.1: Create your own skill and invoke it

Test objective: write a skill by hand, see it indexed and use it as a slash command.

Prerequisites and setup: project from Lab 2.1 (~/hermes-course/day2/project, a git repository). Make an initial commit:

cd ~/hermes-course/day2/project
git add -A && git -c user.name=course -c user.email=course@example.com commit -qm "initial"

Step by step:

  1. Create the skill (this Git status report skill runs git status --short, git log --oneline -5 and git diff --stat, then answers in four sections):
    mkdir -p ~/.hermes/skills/course/git-report
cat > ~/.hermes/skills/course/git-report/SKILL.md << 'EOF2'
---
name: git-report
description: Summarize the repository Git state in English
version: 1.0.0
metadata:
  hermes:
    tags: [git, report]
    category: course
    requires_toolsets: [terminal]
---

# Git status report

## When to Use
When the user asks for a summary of the current repository state.

## Procedure
1. Run `git status --short` and `git log --oneline -5`.
2. Run `git diff --stat`.
3. Answer in English with these sections: "Branch", "Pending changes", "Latest commits", "Suggested next step".

## Pitfalls
- Outside a Git repository, say so and stop. Do not run `git init`.

## Verification
The answer contains all four sections above.
EOF2
  2. Confirm indexing:
    hermes skills list | grep -i git-report
  3. Change something in the repo: echo "# test" >> calc.py
  4. In hermes (in the project directory), run:
    /git-report
    • If the session was already open before you created the skill, run /reload-skills first.
    • Expected: the agent runs the git commands and answers with the four sections.
  5. Test automatic discovery in a new session (no slash): Give me a summary of the repository state. — observe whether the agent picks the skill.
  6. Preloading: hermes chat -s git-report --oneshot -q "Write the report."

Success criterion: skill listed; /git-report produces the four sections.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Skill doesn't show up Invalid YAML frontmatter / file in the wrong place Validate the YAML; path ~/.hermes/skills/<cat>/<name>/SKILL.md
Slash command doesn't exist Session opened earlier /reload-skills
Skill hidden requires_toolsets not satisfied Enable the terminal toolset
Name conflict Same-name skill with higher precedence Rename

Cleanup: keep it for the final project, or rm -rf ~/.hermes/skills/course/git-report.

Extra challenge: use /learn how to generate the Git report we just made, including a count of changed files and compare the skill the agent generates with yours. Enable skills.write_approval: true beforehand and review with /skills pending and /skills diff <id>.

← Lab 3.2 overview15 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 3

Lab 3.2: Install a Hub skill with inspection and auditing

Test objective: practice the safe installation flow for third-party skills.

Step by step:

  1. hermes skills browse --source official — browse and note a slug.
  2. hermes skills inspect official/mcp/fastmcp — read the content before installing (slug cited in the official docs; availability in the catalog (to be validated) on the day).
  3. hermes skills install official/mcp/fastmcp — observe the security scan result.
  4. hermes skills list --source hub — confirm.
  5. hermes skills audit — re-scan all hub skills.
  6. cat ~/.hermes/skills/.hub/audit.log | tail -5 (the path is documented; format (to be validated)).

Success criterion: skill inspected, installed, listed and audited.

Common errors: nonexistent slug (use what shows up in browse/search); scan blocked it (don't use --force without reviewing); Skills Hub blocked by a corporate network (FAQ: "403 / blocked").

Cleanup: hermes skills uninstall fastmcp.

Extra challenge: hermes skills search react --source skills-sh and discuss the trust levels of the sources.

← Lab 3.3 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 3

Lab 3.3: Filesystem MCP with a tool filter

Test objective: connect a stdio MCP server, verify discovery and reduce the surface with a whitelist.

Prerequisites and setup: Node/npx working (node --version, npx --version); allowed folder:

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day3/docs
echo "Vacation policy: 30 calendar days." > ~/hermes-course/day3/docs/policies.txt

Step by step:

  1. Add the server (--args must be the last parameter):
    hermes mcp add course_fs --command npx --args -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem "$HOME/hermes-course/day3/docs"
    • If the wizard asks for a tool selection, pick all of them for now.
  2. Test the connection and see the discovered tools:
    hermes mcp test course_fs; echo "exit=$?"
hermes mcp list
    • Expected: exit=0 and the server's tool list (write down the exact names — they change between package versions; e.g., list directory, read file, write file).
  3. In hermes: Which MCP tools are available now? and then Using the course_fs MCP tools, read policies.txt and summarize it.
    • Expected: tools prefixed mcp_course_fs_...; correct summary.
  4. Restrict it to read-only by editing ~/.hermes/config.yaml (use the exact names written down in step 2; the ones below are examples (to be validated)):
    mcp_servers:
  course_fs:
    command: "npx"
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/hermes-course/day3/docs"]
    tools:
      include: [list_directory, read_text_file]
      prompts: false
      resources: false
    (interactive alternative: hermes mcp configure course_fs).
  5. In the session: /reload-mcp. Ask: Using the course_fs MCP, create new.txt with the text "hi".
    • Expected: the agent does not have the MCP write tool. (It may try to use the native write_file tool — discuss: the MCP filter does not restrict native tools; use toolsets/approvals for that.)
  6. Check the logs: hermes logs mcp -n 20.

Success criterion: hermes mcp test returns 0; after the filter, only the included tools show up.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
exit=1 on test npx missing, package won't download, invalid path npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <dir> manually; see hermes logs mcp
exit=3 Name not in the config hermes mcp list
Tools don't show up Filter with the wrong name / no reload Check names; /reload-mcp
Timeout Server slow/crashed Increase timeout/connect_timeout; check server logs

Cleanup: hermes mcp remove course_fs and rm -rf ~/hermes-course/day3/docs/new.txt.

Extra challenge: explore the Nous-approved catalog (hermes mcp catalog) and install a documentation server (e.g., hermes mcp install deepwiki, cited in the docs) with prompts/resources turned off; or add idle_timeout_seconds: 900 and observe the process being recycled.

← Lab 4.1 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 4

Lab 4.1: Telegram bot with an allowlist

Test objective: chat with Hermes via Telegram with access restricted to your user.

Prerequisites and setup: Telegram on your phone; Day 1 labs completed.

Step by step:

  1. In Telegram, open @BotFather → /newbot → name "Hermes Course" → username ending in bot (e.g., hermes_course_<yourname>_bot). Keep the token.
  2. Open @userinfobot and write down your numeric ID.
  3. Configure:
    hermes gateway setup
    (choose Telegram; enter token and ID) — or manually:
    hermes config set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN "123456789:ABC..."
hermes config set TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS "YOUR_NUMERIC_ID"
  4. Start the gateway:
    hermes gateway status
# if a gateway/service is already running:
hermes gateway restart
# otherwise:
hermes gateway run
    • Note: in v0.22 the TUI/Desktop also use the local gateway as their backend; if one is already running, restart applies the new .env (to be validated in your environment).
  5. In Telegram, send /start or "hi" to the bot. Expected: agent reply within seconds.
  6. Send: What is this machine's hostname and how much free disk space is there? — expected: terminal use; if it asks for approval, reply with /approve or /deny.
  7. Set the home channel: send /sethome in the bot chat.
  8. Test denial: ask a colleague to message the bot. Expected: they receive a pairing code (or are ignored, depending on unauthorized_dm_behavior). Optional: approve with hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE> and revoke with hermes pairing revoke telegram <user-id>.

Success criterion: you chat with the bot; a user outside the allowlist cannot use it without pairing.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Silent bot Gateway stopped / wrong token hermes gateway status; hermes logs gateway -n 50
"Unauthorized" for you Used @username instead of the numeric ID Fix TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS
Old messages lost after reboot drop_pending_updates default on cold boot platforms.telegram.extra.drop_pending_on_cold_boot: false
Polling conflict Another process with the same token Stop the other instance
Bot doesn't see messages in a group Privacy mode Adjust in @BotFather /setprivacy

Cleanup: keep the bot for lab 4.2 and the final project. To shut it down: hermes gateway stop; revoke the token in @BotFather with /revoke if it leaked.

Extra challenge: send a voice message to the bot (requires STT configured in hermes tools → voice) (to be validated in your setup); or use hermes send to send a message from the shell to Telegram (no LLM) — exact syntax in hermes send --help (to be validated).

← Lab 4.2 overview20 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 4

Lab 4.2: Cron: monitor with [SILENT] and an LLM-free watchdog

Test objective: create an LLM job that only notifies when something changes, and a script-only job.

Prerequisites: gateway running (Lab 4.1) and home channel set.

Step by step:

  1. Collection script (the agent reasons about its output):
    mkdir -p ~/.hermes/scripts
cat > ~/.hermes/scripts/course-check.py << 'EOF2'
import os, json
f = os.path.expanduser("~/hermes-course/day4/signal.txt")
state = os.path.expanduser("~/.hermes/scripts/.course-check.json")
cur = open(f).read() if os.path.exists(f) else ""
prev = json.load(open(state))["v"] if os.path.exists(state) else None
json.dump({"v": cur}, open(state, "w"))
print("CHANGE DETECTED\n" + cur if prev is not None and prev != cur else "NO_CHANGE")
EOF2
mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day4 && echo "version 1" > ~/hermes-course/day4/signal.txt
  2. Create the LLM job:
    hermes cron create "every 5m" "If the script output says CHANGE DETECTED, explain in English what changed in one sentence. If it says NO_CHANGE, respond with just [SILENT]." --script course-check.py --name "course-monitor" --deliver telegram
    • The docs show --script ~/.hermes/scripts/<file> in /cron add; a relative path inside ~/.hermes/scripts/ is accepted for cron scripts (no-agent docs) — if it is rejected, use the absolute path (to be validated).
  3. Check: hermes cron list and hermes cron status.
  4. Fire it manually twice: hermes cron run course-monitor (accepts the name). First run: initial state → NO_CHANGE → silence.
  5. Change the signal: echo "version 2" > ~/hermes-course/day4/signal.txt and run hermes cron run course-monitor. Expected: a Telegram message explaining the change.
  6. LLM-free job:
    cat > ~/.hermes/scripts/course-disk.sh << 'EOF2'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
usage=$(df -P "$HOME" | awk 'NR==2 {gsub("%","",$5); print $5}')
if [ "$usage" -gt 10 ]; then echo "Course alert: HOME disk usage is ${usage}%"; fi
EOF2
chmod +x ~/.hermes/scripts/course-disk.sh
hermes cron create "every 30m" --no-agent --script course-disk.sh --deliver telegram --name "course-disk"
hermes cron run course-disk
    • Expected (threshold deliberately low, 10%): a Telegram message with no LLM call.
  7. Fleet health: hermes cron doctor; echo "exit=$?".

Success criterion: no message when nothing changes; a message when it does; watchdog delivers without an LLM.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Nothing happens Gateway stopped (agent jobs run inside it) hermes gateway status/restart
blocked_config Invalid provider key or delivery target Fix it; see the one-time alert that was sent
Script refused Outside ~/.hermes/scripts/ or passed as a command Use a file inside that directory
API variables missing in the script Script environment is sanitized (by design) Don't rely on Hermes secrets in the script
Duplicate/excessive messages Prompt without [SILENT] Adjust the prompt

Cleanup:

hermes cron remove course-monitor
hermes cron remove course-disk
rm -f ~/.hermes/scripts/course-check.py ~/.hermes/scripts/.course-check.json ~/.hermes/scripts/course-disk.sh

Extra challenge: create one from the Telegram chat itself: "Every day at 8am, send me a 3-line summary of the most-commented open issues in NousResearch/hermes-agent." and then inspect it with hermes cron list (look at --deliver origin).

← Lab 4.3 overview10 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 4

Lab 4.3: Parallel delegation with structured output

Test objective: observe subagents running in parallel and the summaries they return.

Step by step:

  1. In hermes, in the ~/hermes-course directory:
    Use delegate_task for 3 parallel tasks: (1) count .py files in ~/hermes-course, (2) list .md files in ~/hermes-course, (3) report the Python version available in the terminal. Each task must return JSON with the keys "task" and "result". Then consolidate the results in a table.
  2. Observe: immediate handle, results arriving as messages, final consolidation.
  3. Run /agents to see the subagents (command listed in the slash commands reference; output (to be validated)).

Success criterion: three independent results consolidated.

Common errors: subagent "doesn't know" something from the conversation → pass context explicitly; batch above the limit → tool error (increase delegation.max_concurrent_children).

Cleanup: none.

Extra challenge: ask for the same thing without mentioning delegate_task and see whether the agent decides to delegate on its own.

← Lab 4.4 overview10 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 4

Lab 4.4: API server + isolated profile

Test objective: call Hermes via the OpenAI-compatible API and create an isolated profile.

Step by step:

  1. Enable the API:
    hermes config set API_SERVER_ENABLED true
hermes config set API_SERVER_KEY "$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
hermes gateway restart      # or: hermes gateway run
    • Expected in the log: [API Server] API server listening on http://127.0.0.1:8642.
  2. Call it:
    KEY=$(grep '^API_SERVER_KEY=' ~/.hermes/.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"')
curl -s http://localhost:8642/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "hermes-agent", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply only: API OK"}]}'
    • Expected: JSON in Chat Completions format with the answer.
  3. Create an isolated profile: hermes profile create course --clone. Important: the clone copies .env, including TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and API_SERVER_ENABLED — and in v0.22 the single gateway activates a new profile's bots without a restart. Remove them from the clone immediately: course config unset TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and course config unset API_SERVER_ENABLED (two profiles cannot use the same token; a secondary profile must not open its own api_server). Then run course chat --oneshot -q "Who am I, according to your memory?" — expected: memory cloned from the default profile.
  4. hermes profile list and hermes gateway list.

Success criterion: answer via curl; course profile created and working.

Common errors: 401 → wrong key; connection refused → gateway not restarted or API_SERVER_ENABLED missing; quotes in .env — adjust KEY to match the file.

Cleanup:

hermes config unset API_SERVER_ENABLED
hermes config unset API_SERVER_KEY
hermes gateway restart

Remove the test profile: hermes profile delete course -y (the final project uses a new profile, ops).

Extra challenge: connect Open WebUI to the endpoint ("Open WebUI" guide in the messaging docs) or use --format stream-json in a script that consumes the events.

← Lab 5.1 overview15 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 5

Lab 5.1: Hardening: manual approval, deny rule and protected writes

Test objective: demonstrate that deny rules block even harmless commands that match, that manual mode asks, and that secret files are protected.

Prerequisites: working installation; directory ~/hermes-course/day5.

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day5 && cd ~/hermes-course/day5
cp ~/.hermes/config.yaml ~/hermes-course/day5/config.yaml.bak

Step by step:

  1. Edit ~/.hermes/config.yaml and append (or merge with an existing approvals block):
    approvals:
  mode: manual
  timeout: 300
  deny:
    - "*course-denied*"
    - "git push --force*"
    • Always quote them: an unquoted leading * is a YAML error. Deny changes take effect immediately.
  2. In hermes: Run exactly: echo course-denied
    • Expected: command blocked by the deny rule, with no approval prompt.
  3. Run: rm -rf ./nonexistent-folder
    • Expected: in manual, an approval prompt (dangerous rm -rf pattern). Answer deny and watch the agent look for an alternative.
  4. Test write protection: Use write_file to create .env in this directory with the content TEST=1
    • Expected: immediate error (.env files are protected anywhere), no prompt.
  5. Permissions of the real .env:
    chmod 600 ~/.hermes/.env && ls -l ~/.hermes/.env
  6. Test --yolo against deny: hermes --yolo chat --oneshot -q "Run exactly: echo course-denied" — expected: still blocked (deny survives yolo).

Success criterion: steps 2, 4 and 6 blocked; step 3 asks for approval.

Common errors: invalid YAML (indentation/quotes) → hermes doctor / hermes config check; deny doesn't match because of text differences (globs are case-insensitive and match the whole command — use * at both ends).

Cleanup: cp ~/hermes-course/day5/config.yaml.bak ~/.hermes/config.yaml.

Extra challenge: set HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT="$HOME/hermes-course:$HOME/.hermes" in a session's environment (export ... && hermes) and ask it to write to ~/Desktop/test.txt — expected: blocked. Run hermes approvals suggest and discuss the proposals.

← Lab 5.2 overview10 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 5

Lab 5.2: Checkpoints and rollback

Test objective: undo destructive changes made by the agent.

Setup:

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/day5/rb && cd ~/hermes-course/day5/rb
printf 'original line\n' > data.txt

Step by step:

  1. hermes chat --checkpoints
  2. Replace all content in data.txt with "destroyed content".
  3. cat data.txt in another terminal — expected: content changed.
  4. In the session: /rollback → lists checkpoints; /rollback diff 1 → preview; /rollback 1 → restores.
  5. cat data.txt — expected: original line.
  6. hermes checkpoints status.

Success criterion: file restored to the original.

Common errors: checkpoints disabled (--checkpoints missing); different checkpoint number (use the one /rollback lists).

Cleanup: rm -rf ~/hermes-course/day5/rb; optionally hermes checkpoints prune.

Extra challenge: enable it globally (hermes config set checkpoints.enabled true) and test with git reset --hard in a test repo.

← Lab 5.3 overview15 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 5

Lab 5.3: Security shell hook (pre_tool_call)

Test objective: write your own guardrail that blocks terminal commands containing a forbidden word.

Step by step:

  1. Create the script:
    mkdir -p ~/.hermes/agent-hooks
cat > ~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py << 'EOF2'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, sys
payload = json.load(sys.stdin)
cmd = (payload.get("tool_input") or {}).get("command", "") or ""
if "forbidden-secret" in cmd:
    print(json.dumps({"decision": "block", "reason": "Blocked by course policy"}))
else:
    print("{}")
EOF2
chmod +x ~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py
  2. Register it in ~/.hermes/config.yaml:
    hooks:
  pre_tool_call:
    - matcher: "terminal"
      command: "~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py"
      timeout: 10
      fail_closed: true
  3. Test offline with a synthetic payload:
    cat > /tmp/course-payload.json << 'EOF2'
{"hook_event_name": "pre_tool_call", "tool_name": "terminal", "tool_input": {"command": "echo forbidden-secret"}, "session_id": "test", "cwd": "/tmp", "profile": "default", "extra": {}}
EOF2
hermes hooks list
hermes hooks test pre_tool_call --for-tool terminal --payload-file /tmp/course-payload.json
hermes hooks doctor
    • Expected: the parsed line shows the block.
  4. Live test: hermes → accept the hook consent prompt (first time) → Run: echo forbidden-secret → expected: blocked with the hook's message. Run: echo allowed → runs normally.

Success criterion: block in the synthetic test and in the real session; an ordinary command passes.

Common errors:

Symptom Cause Fix
Hook doesn't run No consent (gateway/cron don't ask) Run interactive hermes chat once, or --accept-hooks
Everything blocked fail_closed + broken script (invalid JSON, no exec bit) hermes hooks doctor; chmod +x
Event ignored Wrong event name "Did you mean…" message; use pre_tool_call

Cleanup: remove the hooks: block from config.yaml, hermes hooks revoke "~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py", rm ~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py /tmp/course-payload.json.

Extra challenge: a post_tool_call hook that logs every write_file (see the examples in the Hooks docs), or a pre_llm_call hook that injects {"context": "Today is <date>"}.

← Lab 5.4 overview15 min

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 5

Lab 5.4: Docker sandbox and gateway in a container

Test objective: move command execution into a container and run the gateway in Docker.

Prerequisites: Docker running (docker info).

Part A — Docker backend for the terminal:

  1. hermes config set terminal.backend docker
hermes config set terminal.docker_forward_env '[]'
    • The value of docker_forward_env is a list; pass a YAML literal. The documented default image is nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop.
  2. hermes → Run uname -a and cat /etc/os-release and tell me where you are running. — expected: information about the Linux container, not your macOS.
  3. Install the cowsay package with pip and run it. → then, in the same session, /new and Run cowsay hi — expected: the package persists (single persistent container per process).
  4. docker ps — see the sandbox container.

Part B — gateway in Docker (optional, if there is time/a VPS):

  1. mkdir -p ~/hermes-docker-data
docker run -it --rm -v ~/hermes-docker-data:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent setup
docker run -d --name hermes-course --restart unless-stopped \
  -v ~/hermes-docker-data:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent gateway run
docker logs -f hermes-course
    • Use a separate data directory (~/hermes-docker-data) and a different bot token from Lab 4.1 so it does not conflict with the local gateway.

Success criterion: commands run in the container; (B) gateway starts and answers in the chat.

Common errors: Docker stopped → "Docker backend not connecting" (FAQ); two gateways with the same token → conflict; VPS web console corrupting :/@ → use SSH.

Cleanup:

hermes config set terminal.backend local
docker rm -f hermes-course 2>/dev/null; rm -rf ~/hermes-docker-data

Extra challenge: container_persistent: false (container per session) and compare; hermes egress setup && hermes egress start (credential proxy) (to be validated on your OS).

← Lab 5.5 overview5–10 min, in pairs

LAB MATERIAL · DAY 5

Lab 5.5: Troubleshooting drill

Test objective: diagnose injected failures using the method from 7.9.

Step by step (the instructor injects one failure at a time, with a backup first: hermes backup -q -l before-drill):

  1. Nonexistent model: hermes config set model.default model/does-not-exist → the student runs hermes chat --oneshot -q hi, reads the error, uses hermes doctor/hermes model to fix it.
  2. Broken YAML: cp ~/.hermes/config.yaml /tmp/config.yaml.ok && printf 'approvals:\n deny:\n - *unquoted*\n' >> ~/.hermes/config.yaml (an unquoted leading * is a YAML error, according to the docs) → the student runs hermes doctor / hermes config check, finds the line and fixes it (or cp /tmp/config.yaml.ok ~/.hermes/config.yaml). Exact diagnostic message (to be validated).
  3. Interactive shell init: temporarily add read -p "x" to the end of ~/.bashrc (Linux) → agent commands hang/time out → fix with the non-interactive shell guard and remove the line.
  4. Isolate the setup: hermes chat --safe-mode --model <a-valid-model> -q "hi" works even with broken config.
  5. Collect evidence: hermes logs errors -n 30, hermes dump.

Success criterion: each failure identified and fixed in < 3 min using the official tools.

Cleanup: restore config/backup (hermes import <zip> restores a full backup; for the quick snapshot, revert the keys manually with hermes config unset/set) and remove the line from .bashrc.

Extra challenge: use hermes security audit and interpret the report.

← Capstone overviewFINAL PROJECT

LAB MATERIAL · CAPSTONE

Repository operations assistant

Suggested duration: 60–90 min (can take an extended Hour 2 on Day 5 or be homework). For slides: 1 problem-statement slide + 1 architecture slide; the lab script below goes into the appendix.

Test objective: build, in an isolated profile, an agent that knows a repository's rules, generates a daily report via your own skill, reads documentation via MCP with a minimal surface, delivers to Telegram only when there is news, runs with production guardrails and can be queried via API.

Target architecture:

Telegram (allowlist) ──► Gateway ──► profile "ops"
                                      ├─ SOUL.md (ops persona, English)
                                      ├─ AGENTS.md in the repository (rules)
                                      ├─ skill git-report (Lab 3.1)
                                      ├─ MCP ops_docs (read-only, include)
                                      ├─ daily cron at 08:00 with [SILENT]
                                      ├─ approvals manual + deny + hook guard
                                      └─ terminal.backend docker
API server (localhost:8642) ──► same gateway (programmatic query)

Prerequisites and setup: Labs 2.1, 3.1, 3.3, 4.1, 5.1, 5.3 and 5.4 mastered; Docker running; Telegram bot from Lab 4.1; test repository:

mkdir -p ~/hermes-course/final/repo ~/hermes-course/final/docs && cd ~/hermes-course/final/repo
git init -q && printf 'print("v1")\n' > main.py
cat > AGENTS.md << 'EOF2'
# Final repository rules
- Python 3. Do not change files outside this repository.
- Always write reports in English, at most 10 lines.
EOF2
git add -A && git -c user.name=course -c user.email=course@example.com commit -qm initial
echo "Runbook: on a deployment failure, run rollback and notify the channel." > ~/hermes-course/final/docs/runbook.md

Step by step:

  1. Isolated profile:
    hermes profile create ops --clone
hermes profile list
    • Right after that, avoid token/API conflicts inherited from the default: ops config unset TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and ops config unset API_SERVER_ENABLED (the ops profile's own bot comes in step 7).
    • Expected: ops command available (alias = hermes -p ops under the hood); the profile inherited config, .env, SOUL.md, skills (including git-report, if kept from Lab 3.1) and memory.
  2. Persona: edit ~/.hermes/profiles/ops/SOUL.md appending: "You are the course operations assistant. Answer in English and be direct." ("You are the course's operations assistant. Answer in English, objectively.")
  3. Skill: confirm with ops skills list | grep git-report (if it isn't there, recreate it at ~/.hermes/profiles/ops/skills/course/git-report/SKILL.md with the content from Lab 3.1).
  4. Read-only MCP:
    ops mcp add ops_docs --command npx --args -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem "$HOME/hermes-course/final/docs"
ops mcp test ops_docs
ops mcp configure ops_docs     # retain listing/reading tools only
  5. Guardrails in ~/.hermes/profiles/ops/config.yaml:
    approvals:
  mode: manual
  deny:
    - "git push --force*"
    - "*course-denied*"
checkpoints:
  enabled: true
terminal:
  backend: docker
  docker_forward_env: []
  docker_volumes:
    - "/Users/YOUR_USERNAME/hermes-course/final/repo:/workspace/repo"
hooks:
  pre_tool_call:
    - matcher: "terminal"
      command: "~/.hermes/agent-hooks/course-guard.py"
      timeout: 10
      fail_closed: true
    • Recreate the hook script from Lab 5.3 if it was removed. Adjust the volume path (on Linux, /home/YOUR_USERNAME/...). The ~ path in the hook's command refers to your HOME — the hook runs on the host, not in the container (to be validated).
    • With the Docker backend, the repository appears at /workspace/repo inside the sandbox.
  6. Interactive test (accepting the hook):
    ops chat
    • cd /workspace/repo and run /git-report (or /git-report asking it to use /workspace/repo) → report with 4 sections.
    • Using the ops_docs MCP, what does the runbook say to do on a deployment failure? → answer based on runbook.md.
    • Run: echo forbidden-secret → blocked by the hook.
  7. Telegram for the ops profile: the cloned profile inherited the .env with the same TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN as the default — the FAQ is explicit: two profiles cannot share the same token. Create a second bot in @BotFather and save it in the profile: ops config set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN "<new-token>" and ops config set TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS "<your-id>". Restart: hermes gateway restart (v0.22: one gateway serves all profiles) and confirm with hermes gateway list. In the new bot, send /sethome.
  8. Daily cron with smart silence:
    ops cron create "0 8 * * *" "Load the git-report skill procedure: in the repository at /workspace/repo run git status --short and git log --oneline -5. If there are no uncommitted changes, respond with just [SILENT]. Otherwise send the report in English, max 10 lines." --skill git-report --name "ops-daily" --deliver telegram
ops cron list
    • Test: ops cron run ops-daily with no changes → silence; then echo 'print("v2")' >> ~/hermes-course/final/repo/main.py and ops cron run ops-daily → report on Telegram.
    • Note: cron uses approvals.cron_mode: deny by default; git status is not a dangerous command, so it should run.
  9. API: in a multi-profile gateway (v0.22), the listener is the default profile's api_server, and the other profiles are served through the prefix /p/<profile>/v1/... (Multi-profile gateways docs). The secondary profile must not enable its own api_server. Therefore: enable API_SERVER_ENABLED/API_SERVER_KEY on the default (Lab 4.4), set ops config set API_SERVER_KEY "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" (the docs say the key in the secondary's .env "wires the credential without starting a listener"), restart the gateway and call:
    curl -s http://localhost:8642/p/ops/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ops profile API_SERVER_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "hermes-agent", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the runbook using MCP ops_docs"}]}'
    • Which key authenticates the /p/ops/ path (the default's or ops's) (to be validated).
  10. Operations: ops backup -q -l final-project (quick snapshot), hermes cron status, ops logs errors -n 20, ops doctor.

Test data/inputs: main.py, AGENTS.md, runbook.md; the print("v2") change to trigger the report.

Expected result per step: (1) profile created; (4) test exit 0; (6) three correct behaviors; (7) ops bot answers; (8) silence → report after a change; (9) JSON answer; (10) clean diagnostics.

Success criterion (assessment checklist):

  • Isolated ops profile with its own persona.
  • Skill invocable and used by the cron job.
  • MCP with a minimal surface (read-only).
  • Cron silent with no changes and delivering when there are changes.
  • Manual approvals + deny + active hook; commands running in the container.
  • Telegram with an allowlist, bot dedicated to the profile.
  • API answering locally.
  • ops doctor with no pending issues.

Common errors and fixes:

Symptom Cause Fix
ops bot doesn't answer Same token as the default / gateway not reloaded Its own token; hermes gateway restart
Cron doesn't fire Gateway stopped; job blocked_config hermes cron status; fix the config
Empty report Docker volume not mounted Check docker_volumes and docker ps
Hook doesn't run in cron/gateway No non-interactive consent HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1 or manual allowlist
MCP with no tools Overly strict filter ops mcp configure ops_docs

Environment cleanup:

ops cron remove ops-daily
ops mcp remove ops_docs
hermes profile delete ops -y
hermes gateway restart
rm -rf ~/hermes-course/final

Revoke the extra bot's token in @BotFather (/revoke) if you won't reuse it.

Variation/extra challenge:

  • Distribute the ops agent as a profile distribution (git repository + hermes profile install) to a colleague.
  • Add a reviewer subagent via delegate_task with an output_schema that classifies changes (low/medium/high risk).
  • Switch the cron provider to a cheaper model with hermes cron edit ops-daily --provider <p> --model <m>.

REFERENCE · v0.22.5

Quick command cheat sheet

# Installation and health
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
hermes --version ; hermes doctor ; hermes dump ; hermes update --check
# Provider and conversation
hermes model ; hermes setup ; hermes setup --portal
hermes ; hermes --tui ; hermes -c ; hermes -r <id|title>
hermes chat --oneshot -q "..." ; hermes chat -q "..." --format stream-json
# Configuration
hermes config show|get|set|unset|check|migrate|path|env-path
hermes tools ; hermes tools --summary ; hermes chat --toolsets "file,terminal"
# Sessions, memory, learning
hermes sessions list|browse|export|prune|stats ; hermes journey list|edit|delete
# Skills and MCP
hermes skills browse|search|inspect|install|list|audit|uninstall|check|update
hermes mcp add|list|test|configure|remove|catalog|install
# Gateway, cron, profiles
hermes gateway setup|run|start|stop|restart|status|install|list
hermes pairing approve <platform> <code>
hermes cron create|list|edit|pause|resume|run|remove|status|doctor
hermes profile create|list|use|delete|export|import
# Security and operations
hermes hooks list|test|revoke|doctor ; hermes approvals suggest
hermes checkpoints ; hermes backup ; hermes import <zip> ; hermes security audit
hermes logs [agent|errors|gateway|mcp|update] -f --since 1h
hermes pause ; hermes resume ; hermes chat --safe-mode --model <m>

Most-used slash commands: /help, /new, /model, /tools, /skills, /memory, /compress, /plan, /learn, /cron, /reload-mcp, /reload-skills, /rollback, /approve, /deny, /sethome, /personality, /usage, /journey.
